lesson.8_1.title: Phishing and Tricks
lesson.8_1.gut.prompt: A call says your SIM will be blocked in one hour unless you press 1. What do you do?
lesson.8_1.gut.c1.label: Press 1
lesson.8_1.gut.c1.result: You just connected to a scammer.
lesson.8_1.gut.c2.label: Cut the call
lesson.8_1.gut.bridge: Scammers don't hack computers; they hack human emotions.
lesson.8_1.c1.text: Scammers use urgency. If someone says 'DO IT NOW or you lose your account', it's a scam.
lesson.8_1.c2.text: Phishing is when they send fake links that look like your real bank to steal your passwords.
lesson.8_1.c3.text: They use authority. A scammer might say they are from the Police or Customs and threaten you with 'Digital Arrest'.
lesson.8_1.c4.text: Remember: The real police will never ask you to transfer a 'security deposit' over a video call to clear your name.
lesson.8_1.c5.text: Never share your OTP or UPI PIN. A PIN is only for sending money, never receiving.
lesson.8_1.q1.o1: Sending fake links to steal passwords
lesson.8_1.q1.right: Correct! It's a trick to steal your login details.
lesson.8_1.q1.wrong: Phishing is a scam technique using fake links or emails.
lesson.8_1.q2.prompt: The Police can put you under 'Digital Arrest' via a Skype video call.
lesson.8_1.q2.right: Correct! 'Digital Arrest' does not exist in Indian law.
lesson.8_1.q2.wrong: False! There is no such thing as Digital Arrest.
lesson.8_1.q3.prompt: When should you enter your UPI PIN?
lesson.8_1.q3.right: Correct! Never enter it to receive money.
lesson.8_1.q3.wrong: A UPI PIN is ONLY used when money is leaving your account.
lesson.8_2.title: Investment Scams
lesson.8_2.gut.prompt: An offer promises to double your money in 90 days. Run the 5-point check.
lesson.8_2.gut.c1.label: It's a scam
lesson.8_2.gut.c2.label: Seems fine
lesson.8_2.gut.bridge: Here is how to spot a bad investment.
lesson.8_2.c1.text: Check 1: Is it registered with SEBI, RBI, or IRDAI?
lesson.8_2.c2.text: Check 2: Is the promise realistic? Guaranteed doubling is a scam.
lesson.8_2.c3.text: Check 3: Does the money go to a company account, not a personal UPI?
lesson.8_2.c4.text: Check 4: Is there an easy way to withdraw money?
lesson.8_2.c5.text: Check 5: Can you explain it simply to a friend?
lesson.8_2.q1.prompt: Which agency registers real stock market investments?
lesson.8_2.q1.wrong: SEBI is the market regulator in India.
lesson.8_2.q2.prompt: Guaranteed 50% monthly returns on crypto are normal.
lesson.8_2.q2.right: Correct! High guaranteed returns are always scams.
lesson.8_2.q2.wrong: False! High guaranteed returns are huge red flags.
lesson.8_2.q3.prompt: If you fail multiple points on the 5-point check, what do you do?
lesson.8_2.q3.o1: Stop and ask a trusted adult
lesson.8_2.q3.o2: Invest a small amount to test it
lesson.8_2.q3.right: Correct! Never invest just to test it.
lesson.8_2.q3.wrong: Stop and ask an adult. Testing it will lose you money.
lesson.8_3.title: Protect & Report
lesson.8_3.gut.prompt: You clicked a bad link and money left your account. What do you do first?
lesson.8_3.gut.c1.label: Call 1930
lesson.8_3.gut.c2.label: Delete the app
lesson.8_3.gut.bridge: Here is exactly what to do if you are scammed.
lesson.8_3.c1.text: Step 1: Stop communicating. Do not pay them any 'recovery fees'.
lesson.8_3.c2.text: Step 2: Call your bank to freeze your account and cards.
lesson.8_3.c3.text: Step 3: Dial 1930 immediately. If reported fast, the cyber cell can freeze the stolen money.
lesson.8_3.c4.text: Step 4: Take screenshots of all chats and receipts. Report at cybercrime.gov.in.
lesson.8_3.c5.text: Step 5: Tell someone. Scammers rely on your shame to stay quiet. Tell a trusted adult.
lesson.8_3.q1.prompt: What is the national cybercrime helpline number?
lesson.8_3.q2.prompt: You should pay a small fee to the scammer to 'release' your stolen money.
lesson.8_3.q2.right: Correct! That is just a second scam.
lesson.8_3.q2.wrong: False! Recovery fees are always part of the scam.
lesson.8_3.q3.prompt: Why should you tell a trusted adult?
lesson.8_3.q3.o1: Because scammers rely on your shame to stay hidden
lesson.8_3.q3.right: Correct! Breaking the silence stops scammers.
lesson.8_3.q3.wrong: Scammers rely on shame to keep you from reporting.
